landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

technical.intro: This page collects the model, tuning, and local-workflow details behind the browser editor. It is written for users who want pinned weights, repeatable settings, lower-VRAM variants, or a local ComfyUI graph.
technical.weights.title: Model weight and version guidance
technical.weights.body: Prefer v1.2 when it is available. It is the recommended build on the model card and adds reference sheets, swaps, inpainting, outpainting, virtual try-on, and FIT geometry. Confirm the version pinned by the hosted Space before comparing results across sessions.
technical.settings.note: Treat these values as starting points from the public model card and node changelog, not universal guarantees. Change one control at a time and compare against the source image.
technical.comparison.note: The hosted editor is best for quick prompt tests. A local graph is better when you need exact versions, repeatable seeds, batches, private infrastructure, or additional LoRAs.

guide.meta.title: Krea2 Identity Edit Guide — How to Use It (Step by Step)
guide.meta.description: Complete guide to Krea2 Identity Edit. Learn to restage characters, swap backgrounds, and do virtual try-ons with plain-English instructions.
guide.h1: Krea2 Identity Edit: The Complete Guide
guide.intro: Krea2 Identity Edit is a community LoRA workflow for changing an image while anchoring the referenced person's likeness. It accepts a source image plus a natural-language edit instruction. Use it for restaging, local replacement, compositing, inpainting, and virtual try-on without rebuilding the subject from scratch.
guide.needs.title: What you need before starting
guide.needs.body: For the online workflow, you only need a modern browser and a source image you have permission to edit. Prepare the following before entering the shared GPU queue.
guide.needs.items: A clear source~~Use a sharp, well-lit image with one primary subject and a face large enough to inspect.|||One intended change~~Decide what must change and what must remain untouched before you write the prompt.|||A comparison habit~~Keep the source visible so you can check eyes, face shape, skin details, clothing marks, and unintended changes.
guide.tutorial.title: Step-by-step Krea2 Identity Edit tutorial
guide.tutorial.intro: Follow this six-step loop for a reliable first result. Change one variable at a time so you know what improved or damaged likeness.
guide.tutorial.items: Open the online workspace~~Go to the identity editor and wait for the embedded Space to finish loading. Open it full-screen if the page is narrow.|||Upload the source image~~Choose a clear portrait or character image. Avoid heavy compression, motion blur, and multiple similar faces.|||Write a concrete prompt~~Use a trained action such as replace, recolor, restage, add, or remove. Mention only what you want changed.|||Choose a practical starting recipe~~For common restages and replacements, start with a short Turbo-style run. Use the exposed defaults before tuning advanced controls.|||Generate and audit identity~~Compare the face, hairline, skin marks, silhouette, and any detail you expected to remain fixed.|||Refine one variable~~Shorten the prompt if the edit spreads too far. Increase reference strength carefully if likeness drifts, then generate again.
guide.prompts.title: Prompt examples that work
guide.prompts.intro: These templates are deliberately concrete. Replace the bracketed detail, keep one main verb, and leave preserved details out of the instruction.
guide.prompts.items: Background~~Create a photo of this person at a night market with warm lantern light.|||Studio restage~~Place this person in a minimal photo studio with a soft gray backdrop.|||Outfit color~~Recolor the jacket to rust orange while keeping its material and shape.|||Virtual try-on~~Replace the shirt with a tailored navy blazer over a white T-shirt.|||Object replacement~~Replace the coffee cup with a small ceramic bowl.|||Object addition~~Add a black leather shoulder bag to this person.|||Season change~~Restage this person on a snowy street in soft morning light.|||Cinematic light~~Relight the scene with a cool window key light and warm practical lights.|||Pose and framing~~Create a waist-up editorial portrait of this person looking over their shoulder.|||Character composite~~Place the person from image 2 naturally into the street scene from image 1.|||Hair edit~~Change the hairstyle to a short textured bob while keeping the same face.|||Clean background~~Replace the background with a clean off-white wall and soft floor shadow.
guide.problems.title: Common problems and fixes
guide.problems.intro: Most failed edits come from an overloaded prompt, a weak source, or a setting outside the model's comfortable range.
guide.problems.items: The face looks like a relative, not the same person.~~Use a sharper source, shorten the prompt, and increase reference fidelity gradually. Extreme changes in angle can still alter facial geometry.|||The image turns into a split composition.~~Reference grounding may be too strong or the input order may be wrong. Return to defaults and verify scene-first, person-second ordering for two-reference composites.|||The edit changes too much.~~Ask for one local change with a direct replacement or recolor verb. Remove style language that affects the entire frame.|||Removing an object keeps failing.~~Removal is harder than adding or replacing. Try the Raw-style recipe when available, simplify the surrounding scene, and expect a few reruns.
guide.try.title: Try it online without ComfyUI
guide.try.body: Use the browser editor first to validate your source image and prompt. You can move to a local ComfyUI workflow later if you need pinned weights, batch output, or stacked LoRAs.

image.meta.title: Free Identity Preserving Image Editor — Edit Photos Without Losing Faces
image.meta.description: Identity preserving AI image editor. Upload a photo, give a plain-English instruction, and get edited results while keeping the person's identity intact.
image.intro: Edit your photos. Keep the people. Change everything else with a plain-English instruction in a free browser workspace.
image.what.title: What is identity-preserving editing?
image.what.body: Identity-preserving image editing changes a scene, outfit, object, pose, or visual attribute while using the source person as an identity reference. Unlike a general text-to-image regeneration, the goal is not to invent a similar person; it is to retain recognizable facial and character cues across the edit. Results still need human review because no generative model guarantees an exact match.
image.use.title: Identity-preserving editing use cases
image.use.intro: The workflow is most useful when visual continuity matters more than generating a completely new subject.
image.use.items: Portrait restaging~~Move the same person between locations, lighting setups, and camera treatments for campaign concepts.|||Virtual wardrobe~~Explore clothing silhouettes and colorways without losing the model who anchors the original photo.|||Character continuity~~Keep a recognizable protagonist across storyboard frames, key art, and visual development.|||Local corrections~~Replace props, recolor garments, or clean backgrounds while leaving unmentioned regions as stable as possible.
image.compare.title: How it compares to regular AI editors
image.compare.intro: Both tools generate pixels, but they optimize for different outcomes. Choose identity-preserving editing when continuity is part of the brief.
image.compare.rows: Primary goal~~Create a plausible edited image~~Keep the referenced person recognizable|||Face behavior~~May regenerate or drift~~Anchored to source identity cues|||Best input~~Text prompt or source image~~Clear source person plus a focused instruction|||Best use~~Broad restyles and exploration~~Restaging, try-on, composites, and continuity
image.faq.title: Identity-preserving editor FAQ
image.faq.intro: What to expect before you upload a photo.
image.faq.items: Is this the same as face swap?~~No. Face swap usually replaces one face region. Identity-preserving editing can restage the whole image while using the source person as a reference.|||Can it keep clothes and change only the background?~~Yes, that is a strong use case. State only the new background and avoid extra style instructions that could alter clothing.|||Can I use more than one person?~~Single-subject images are the safest starting point. Multi-person composites can blend identities, so build complex scenes in controlled passes.|||Is the editor free and private?~~The embedded community Space is free to try. Your file is processed by that third-party Space, so do not upload sensitive images and review its current terms.

vs.meta.title: Krea2 vs Krea AI Edit — Which Editor Should You Use?
vs.meta.description: Compare Krea2 Identity Edit with Krea AI Edit. See the differences in identity preservation, regional editing, setup, models, control, and cost.
vs.intro: Krea2 Identity Edit and Krea AI Edit solve overlapping problems through different products. This site offers a focused community Identity Edit workflow built on the open Krea 2 stack; Krea AI is the official, broader browser suite with region tools and multiple editing models.
vs.status.title: The short answer
vs.status.body: Choose Krea2 Identity Edit when your main job is preserving a referenced person while restaging, replacing clothing, or compositing a character. Choose Krea AI when you want a polished all-in-one canvas for regional selection, object movement, lighting, camera, enhancement, generation, video, and asset management.
vs.compare.title: Krea2 Identity Edit vs Krea AI Edit
vs.compare.intro: The comparison is about workflow, not a universal winner. Krea AI is an official multi-model creative product; the tool on this site is a narrower community workflow centered on identity continuity.
vs.compare.rows: Primary focus~~Identity-preserving restaging and character edits~~General image editing inside a full creative suite|||Editing interface~~Prompt plus source/reference images~~Canvas with selections, brush, annotations, crop, lighting, camera, and palette controls|||Models~~Community Identity Edit workflow on the open Krea 2 stack~~Multiple editing models available inside Krea's product|||ComfyUI~~Not required for the hosted tool; optional for local control~~Not required; official browser application|||Local control~~Possible through the open model and community ComfyUI workflow~~Cloud product; local model graphs are not the core experience|||Account and usage~~Embedded community Space; availability follows its shared GPU queue~~Krea account with free daily compute and paid tiers|||Best for~~Focused likeness tests, prompt research, and open workflow experiments~~Broader production editing, iteration, generation, video, and asset workflows
vs.choose.title: Which Krea editor fits your job?
vs.choose.intro: Start from the output you need, then choose the smaller workflow that can produce it.
vs.choose.items: Choose Krea2 Identity Edit~~Use it when a particular face or character must remain recognizable across a new background, outfit, pose, or composite—and you want to test the workflow without installing ComfyUI.|||Choose Krea AI Edit~~Use the official Krea product when you need precise regional selections, object movement, annotations, relighting, camera changes, many editing models, and a larger creative workspace.
vs.sources.title: What the official Krea product includes
vs.sources.body: Krea's official Edit documentation lists region changes, annotations, crop or expand, image adjustments, lighting, drawing, camera angle, and color palette controls. Its current product pages also describe multiple editing models and free daily compute. Krea2 Identity Edit is not the official Krea Edit product and this site is not affiliated with Krea.ai.
vs.faq.title: Krea2 vs Krea AI FAQ
vs.faq.intro: Clear up the naming before choosing a workflow.
vs.faq.items: Is Krea2 Identity Edit made by Krea AI?~~No. Krea 2 is Krea's open model family, while the Identity Edit LoRA and hosted workflow used here are community projects.|||Does Krea AI preserve identity?~~Krea offers reference composition and several editing models, but its product is broader than a dedicated Identity Edit workflow. Test your exact face-continuity requirement before choosing.|||Do either of them require ComfyUI?~~No for the browser versions. ComfyUI is only needed if you choose the local, node-based Krea2 Identity Edit workflow.|||Which option is free?~~This site's embedded community Space is free to try when its shared GPU is available. Krea AI currently offers free daily compute with limits; plans and allowances can change.
vs.cta.title: Test identity continuity before choosing
vs.cta.description: Run one source image and one focused edit in Krea2 Identity Edit, then compare the result against the broader workflow you need.
nocomfy.meta.title: Krea2 Edit Without ComfyUI — Use It Directly in Your Browser
nocomfy.meta.description: No ComfyUI, no LoRA setup, no Python. Use Krea2 Identity Edit directly in your browser. Upload an image, type an instruction, and generate.
nocomfy.intro: Skip ComfyUI. Edit directly. Upload a source image, describe one change, and use the hosted Krea2 Identity Edit workflow from your browser.
nocomfy.compare.title: ComfyUI vs browser — what's the difference?
nocomfy.compare.intro: Both routes can reach the same kind of identity edit. The browser optimizes for speed to first test; ComfyUI optimizes for repeatability and control.
nocomfy.compare.rows: Setup~~Open the page and upload an image~~Install ComfyUI, nodes, model files, and dependencies|||Hardware~~Uses the hosted Space GPU~~Uses your compatible local or rented GPU|||Control~~Focused controls exposed by the hosted app~~Full graph, pinned weights, seeds, LoRA stacking, and batch workflows|||Maintenance~~Space owner maintains the environment~~You maintain Python, nodes, models, and updates|||Availability~~Shared queue and uptime can vary~~Available whenever your configured machine is ready|||Best for~~First tests, prompt validation, and occasional edits~~Repeatable production, automation, and advanced tuning
nocomfy.start.title: How to get started in 30 seconds
nocomfy.start.intro: You can reach the Generate step in about 30 seconds with a prepared image. Rendering time depends on the shared GPU queue.
nocomfy.start.items: Upload one clear image~~Choose a sharp single-person photo you have permission to edit.|||Type one concrete instruction~~Ask for one background, clothing, object, pose, or lighting change.|||Press Generate~~Submit the job, wait for the shared GPU, then compare the result with your source.
nocomfy.faq.title: Krea2 without ComfyUI FAQ
nocomfy.faq.intro: What the hosted route removes—and what it does not.
nocomfy.faq.items: Do I need Python or a GPU?~~No. The hosted Space supplies the runtime and GPU; you only need a modern browser.|||Do I need to download the Krea 2 model or LoRA?~~No. The hosted environment already contains its configured workflow and weights.|||Is the browser output instant?~~Submission is fast, but generation is not guaranteed to be instant. Shared GPU queues and Space availability affect wait time.|||When should I move to ComfyUI?~~Move local when you need pinned versions, repeatable seeds, batch generation, custom graphs, private infrastructure, or additional LoRAs.
